children: Mortgage rates reached a fifteen-month high, impacting home sales. All eyes are on the upcoming Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
30-year fixed-rate mortgages averaged 6.76% as of September 10, up from 6.71% last week and 6.35% in the same period a year ago, according to the Weekly Mortgage Applications Survey.
15-year fixed-rate mortgages averaged 6.09%, up from 6.04% a week ago and 5.50% a year ago.
"Mortgage rates are at 15-month highs, straining affordability despite improved housing inventory.

declined last week, with higher rates weighing particularly on refinance activity. Next week's FOMC meeting will be key, as the inflation and economic outlook will help shape the path of rates and homebuyer demand," said Bob Broeksmit, CEO of the Mortgage Bankers Association.
"Mortgage rates and home sales move in opposite directions, so it's not surprising to see a mild dip in home-buying activity due to high mortgage rates,"
National Association of Realtors' chief economist, Lawrence Yun.
"Still, home prices are rising, and existing home sales are actually up 1.6% year-to-date through the first eight months of the year," said Yun.

"Homebuying demand, despite higher interest rates, is no doubt being supported by rising wages, which grew 3.1% in August, along with 643,000 net new jobs added since the start of the year. Job creation and wage growth typically drive housing demand."

"All eyes are on the upcoming Federal Reserve meeting, as a rate cut might have buyers pressing play on home shopping. But, a rate hike could further erode consumer confidence and keep them on pause," said Ali Wolf, chief economist at NewHomeSource and Zonda.

title: Mortgage rates hit fifteen-month high, home sales impacted
